title: Sales Enablement: Enterprise Prospect Kit — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck Guidance, Pricing, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Riley Chen
content:
Summary:

This prospect-facing kit consolidates Redwood Inference's core positioning, competitive differentiators, recommended pitch flow, pricing guidance for enterprise conversations, representative case studies, and a concise security FAQ to share with prospects. Use this as a single-stop sales play for engineering-led enterprise opportunities (SaaS platform leads, regulated verticals, and platform teams evaluating inference runtimes).

1) One-line positioning and elevator pitch

- One-line: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, cost‑efficient, and reliable LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- 30s elevator: "We help engineering teams ship LLM features with consistent, production-grade performance — low latency, predictable cost, and simple rollouts across hosted, reserved, or private environments. Teams get a single API and observability suite so you can focus on product rather than building inference infrastructure."

2) Value propositions (audience-tailored)

- For Platform/Infrastructure teams:
  - Unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments reduces operational complexity and standardizes SLAs across business units.
  - Predictable throughput with Dedicated capacity and autoscaling policies helps meet SLOs without overprovisioning.

- For Product/ML teams:
  - Transparent cost-per-token and model recommendations to optimize latency/cost tradeoffs.
  - Built-in evals and quality monitoring prevent regressions when switching models or quantization profiles.

- For Security/Compliance stakeholders:
  - Private deployment options (VPC / on-prem) and KMS/HSM integrations plus audit logging and RBAC for enterprise controls.

3) Competitive brief (top competitors and talking points)

- Competitors considered: Large cloud ML endpoints (AWS Sagemaker/Bedrock, GCP Vertex), LLM API providers (OpenAI, Cohere), and self-hosted inference vendors (Replicate/Anyscale/custom runtimes).

- Key differentiation matrix (talking points):
  - Performance predictability: Redwood provides verified performance profiles + dedicated capacity to deliver consistent latency under SLOs.
  - Unified deployment modes: Unlike many cloud-only APIs or purely self-hosted runtimes, Redwood supports the same API and rollout tools across hosted, dedicated, and private.
  - Cost controls: Intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization recommendations reduce unit cost in measurable ways — we can run a quick benchmark against customer workloads.
  - Quality guardrails: Integrated eval harness and regression alerts (by prompt set) reduce product risk when changing models or configs.
  - Enterprise controls: First-class private deployment packaging, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and SOC2-/ISO-aligned controls.

- Objection handling (common asks):
  1. "Why not just use cloud provider endpoints?"
     - Response: Cloud endpoints can be convenient but often lack cost-optimizing primitives (KV caching, batching tuned for chat patterns) and present fragmentation if you need private/on‑prem options. Redwood offers consistent performance profiles and tooling focused on production inference economics.
  2. "Can we self-host cheaper?"
     - Response: Self-hosting can reduce sticker price but shifts engineering effort and risk to your team. Redwood’s Dedicated or Private packages include orchestration, SLAs, and operational tooling that avoid hidden operational costs and accelerate time-to-value.
  3. "What about model coverage?"
     - Response: We maintain a curated model catalog with Redwood-verified profiles, plugin support for customer models, and recommendations (including quantized variants) to balance quality and cost.

4) Pitch deck guidance (recommended flow and slide-level notes)

- 8–12 slide flow (recommended):
  1. Title + customer logo + meeting purpose
  2. 30s elevator + pain validation (specific to prospect: cost, latency, ops burden)
  3. Why inference serving matters (latency, cost, reliability metrics)
  4. Redwood product overview (hosted, Dedicated, Private) + one-liner value props
  5. Architecture snapshot (simple diagram: client -> API + routing -> serving runtime -> GPU fleet / dedicated pools / private VPC)
  6. Performance snapshots & SLO examples (p50/p95 latency, throughput, autoscale behavior)
  7. Cost optimization levers (batching, caching, quantization) with a micro-benchmark example
  8. Security & compliance overview (VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC2)
  9. Case study: 1–2 slides showing impact (throughput, latency, cost delta)
  10. Commercials & next steps (POC plan, trial capacity, SLA options)
  11. Appendix: integration checklist + FAQ

- Slide notes (concise):
  - Use concrete numbers where possible. Example: "Reduced per-call token cost by 32% using prefix caching + 4-bit quantized model in production; p95 latency at 420ms in Dedicated pool for 2k RPS workload".
  - For technical audiences include an appendix with config examples (deployment YAML, autoscale params, sample curl/SDK calls).

5) Pricing guidance (enterprise conversation stage)

- Pricing levers we present during commercial discussions (summary):
  - Hosted API: usage-based pricing (tokens / embeddings) with free-tier credits for evaluation.
  - Dedicated: reserved capacity pricing (monthly/annual), measured by committed GPU-pool units and throughput targets.
  - Private: licensing + support fees for on-prem/VPC deployments; optional professional services for installation and tuning.

- Negotiation tips and common proposals:
  - Offer a time-limited POC with capped spend and success metrics (e.g., p95 latency <= X ms, cost-per-token <= Y) to move from evaluation to commit.
  - For Dedicated deals, propose a 6–12 month ramp with a baseline committed capacity and a burst pool for seasonal spikes.
  - Include an index for model and token usage in the contract to address unexpected growth (prefer tiered discounts rather than unlimited burn).

- Example commercial scenario (talking point for AE):
  "Customer A (SaaS): 10M tokens/day, required p95 < 800ms. Proposal: Dedicated 4-GPU pool with autoscale to 8 GPUs for bursts, 12-month commit. Outcome: estimated 28% lower unit cost vs cloud-managed endpoints and stable p95 latency under traffic profile."

6) Case studies and testimonials (abstracts to customize)

- Case study: Conversational Support Platform (anonymous)
  - Problem: high latency and cost for multi-turn support assistant during peak business hours.
  - Solution: Migrated to Redwood Dedicated, enabled KV/prefix caching, and applied quantized model variant for non-sensitive paths.
  - Results: 45% reduction in average per‑token cost, p95 latency improved from 1.2s to 480ms, and 99.95% uptime during peak windows.

- Case study: Regulated Financial Platform
  - Problem: required private deployment and strict audit trails for model inputs/outputs.
  - Solution: Private deployment in customer VPC, KMS key integration, and audit logging for all inference requests.
  - Results: Successful SOC2 scope extension and production rollout within 10 weeks.

- How to use: Provide a one-page case study PDF + 2–3 slides that can be added to the prospect deck. Include anonymized metrics and a short customer quote.

7) Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers for sales)

Q: Where do you store customer data and logs?
A: By default in hosted deployments logs and telemetry are stored in our managed control plane in region-specific storage; for sensitive customers we offer private deployment options that keep data in the customer VPC or on-prem environment. Audit logs and request traces are configurable and can be forwarded to customer SIEM.

Q: Do you support customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes. We integrate with major KMS providers and can support HSM-backed key management for Private deployments. Keys can be customer-managed to ensure separation of duties.

Q: Can we run Redwood entirely on-prem / air-gapped?
A: Yes. We provide an on-prem packaging option for air-gapped environments; this is typically delivered with a professional services engagement and includes install, validation, and a secure upgrade path.

Q: What certifications and audits do you maintain?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and is actively pursuing ISO 27001. We also provide audit evidence packages and support customer audits through our compliance team.

Q: How do you isolate multi-tenant workloads?
A: Tenant isolation is achieved via dedicated pools for customers that require strict separation. For hosted customers we use logical isolation with strict RBAC, per-tenant network controls, and encrypted storage.

Q: How are models and code updates validated?
A: We run controlled rollouts, canary tests, and automatic rollback policies. Our CI/CD pipeline includes regression evaluation harnesses and quality gates tied to prompt sets and eval metrics.

8) Sales collateral & enablement assets (what to hand the prospect)

- One-page ROI / value memo tailored to vertical (SaaS, FinServ, Healthcare).
- 8–12 slide pitch deck template (editable) with appendix for technical integration.
- Case study one-pagers (anonymized) and 2–3 slide mini decks.
- Security FAQ PDF and SOC2 evidence summary (redacted) for security teams.
- Integration checklist (network, IAM, model onboarding, data residency).

9) Integration checklist (technical pre-sales)

- Network & connectivity:
  - IP allowlist / peering requirements documented
  - VPC endpoints for private deployments
- Auth & keys:
  - API key flow for hosted trials
  - KMS integration plan for Private deployments
- Data residency & retention:
  - Specify retention windows for logs and telemetry
  - Determine whether request/response payloads must be retained or scrubbed
- Model & eval:
  - Identify canonical prompt sets and SLOs for evals
  - Provide sample traffic profile for perf sizing

10) Next steps and ownership

- Recommended POC playbook (3–6 weeks):
  1. Week 0: Kickoff — capture success metrics, network prep, and sample workload
  2. Week 1–2: Integration — API keys, VPC peering (if needed), model onboarding, and smoke tests
  3. Week 2–4: Performance tuning — run workload benchmarks, apply batch/caching suggestions, set autoscale policies
  4. Week 4–6: Validation & handoff — quality evals, reporting dashboard, and commercial review

- Ownership: Account Executive owns commercial cadence; Solutions Engineer owns technical POC and integration tasks; Customer Success Manager will own post-sale onboarding and SLA monitoring.

Appendix: Example curl + YAML snippet (include in appendix slide)

- Example SDK call:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","input":"Summarize customer conversation", "max_tokens":256}'

- Example autoscale YAML (illustrative):
  service: inference-dedicated
  autoscale:
    min_gpus: 2
    target_rps_per_gpu: 500
    scale_out_threshold: 0.85
    scale_in_threshold: 0.25
